headline: Britain tried to build an aircraft carrier out of ice.
slides: German U-boats were sinking Allied ships and steel was in short supply.
Inventor Geoffrey Pyke proposed a giant aircraft carrier made of ice.
Ice mixed with wood pulp. Far stronger than ice, and much slower to melt.
Mountbatten reportedly dropped a block of it into Churchill's bath to prove it floated.
A small test ship was built on Patricia Lake, Alberta. It took three summers to melt.
Costs rose and longer-range planes closed the gap it was meant to cover. What's left lies on the lake bed.
sources: Sources: 99% Invisible, Imperial War Museum, Parks Canada (Patricia Lake), Perutz's wartime reports
